positions.summary: The BC NDP says it will push empty homes onto the rental and sale market through higher speculation taxes and a new tax on unsold condos. In government it has funded middle-income rental construction and rent supplements.
commitments: 2026 platform: Raise the Speculation and Vacancy Tax from 1% to 2% for domestic owners of secondary properties and from 4% to 5% for foreign speculators.
2026 platform: Introduce an Unsold Condo Tax on large developer-owned finished condos vacant and unsold for more than one year, starting at 2% in year two and rising 1% for each additional year.
2026 platform: Aim to unlock up to 5,000 finished condos for people to buy or rent.
In government (Budget 2025): An additional $318 million over three years for BC Builds middle-income rental homes.
In government (Budget 2025): $375 million over three years for rental support programs, raising the average Rental Assistance Program supplement from $400 to $700 per month.
positions.sourceTitle: BC NDP 2026 election platform (bcndp.ca/plan)

positions.summary: The party says it would speed up approvals and reduce costs on new housing; its 2026 campaign pledges to "build homes faster", and its detailed housing measures come from its 2024 platform.
commitments: 2024 platform: Approve homes in months, not years: 6 months for a rezoning and development permit and 3 months for a building permit, with the province issuing permits if a city misses the deadline.
2024 platform: Repeal the BC Step Code, the net-zero building mandate and other provincial costs on new housing.
2024 platform: Repeal Bill 44 (small-scale multi-unit housing zoning) and work with municipalities on their own approach.
2024 platform: Create a $1 billion-per-year Civic Infrastructure Renewal Fund for municipalities whose zoning allows small-scale multi-unit housing on at least two-thirds of residential land.
2024 platform: Conduct a forensic audit of BC Housing, including its relationships with non-profit housing providers.
positions.sourceTitle: Conservative Party of BC 2024 election platform (housing section)

positions.summary: The BC Greens say government, not the private market, is responsible for deeply affordable housing, and propose public funding for non-market homes alongside new renter protections.
commitments: 2026 platform: Restart the Community Housing Fund and Indigenous Housing Fund immediately, with a goal of building and protecting 26,000 housing units per year.
2026 platform: Implement vacancy control, tying allowable rent increases to the unit rather than the tenant.
2026 platform: Protect 2,000 deeply affordable rental homes each year through increased funding for the Rental Protection Fund.
2026 platform: Amend the Residential Tenancy Act to prohibit blanket no-pets clauses in rental agreements.
2026 platform: Create a Residential Tenancy Branch process for renters to seek an annual rent review when market rents in their city are falling.
positions.sourceTitle: BC Greens 2026 platform, "Believe in Better" (October 2026)

positions.summary: CentreBC would set provincial approval deadlines, double BC Builds and reduce costs on rental and below-market housing.
commitments: By January 1, 2028, set a provincial standard of 6 months for rezonings and 8 weeks for building permits, refunding fees if deadlines are missed
Double BC Builds to 20,000 below-market homes by 2031
Cut development cost charges in half on new rental and below-market homes, with $240 million a year to a municipal growth fund and a $125 million a year housing performance fund
Rebate PST on building materials for purpose-built rentals of 4+ homes started 2027-2032
Reach 5,000 prefabricated and BC-made mass-timber homes a year by 2030
positions.sourceTitle: CentreBC 2026 platform, A Balanced Plan for British Columbia (updated 2026-10-16)

positions.summary: OneBC says building and rental rules raise costs and discourage new rental supply, and would remove them.
commitments: Eliminate the BC Energy Step Code, which the party says raises housing costs through green building requirements
Block municipal rent control programs, which the party says discourage new rental units

Petition: introduce legislation for a public inquiry into the province's handling of condo project financing (the party's 'condo bailout' petition), saying developers rather than taxpayers should bear losses
positions.sourceTitle: OneBC, Our Priorities (party policy page, accessed Oct 2026)

positions.summary: The BC NDP proposes lowering fuel and grocery costs through a fuel-tax suspension and margin rules, and extending the ICBC basic insurance rate freeze. In government it removed the consumer carbon tax in 2025.
commitments: 2026 platform: Suspend 10 cents per litre of the provincial motor fuel tax on gasoline and diesel and give the BC Utilities Commission a "price guard" to cap excess fuel margins; the party estimates savings of up to 30 cents per litre.

2026 platform: Cap retail margins on basic groceries (milk, eggs, cheese, butter, poultry), require per-unit pricing and prohibit algorithmic pricing; the party estimates savings of up to $700 a year.
2026 platform: Extend the ICBC basic insurance rate freeze for three more years, to spring 2030.
In government (2025): Set the consumer carbon tax rate to $0 effective April 1, 2025, while keeping carbon pricing for large industrial emitters.
positions.sourceTitle: BC NDP 2026 election platform (bcndp.ca/plan)

positions.summary: The party says it would lower costs mainly by cutting provincial income tax and some sales taxes, and by keeping auto insurance rates low.
commitments: 2026 platform: Raise the basic personal exemption from $13,216 to $32,000, cutting provincial income tax by up to $1,000 a year per worker (about $2,000 for a two-income couple, or $167 a month).
2026 platform: Remove the PST on Canadian beer, wine and spirits for the duration of the U.S. trade war.
2026 platform: Keep ICBC as a public auto-insurance option with service standards and public reporting, expand competition, and give seriously injured people rights to full compensation.
2024 platform: Remove the PST on used cars.
positions.sourceTitle: Conservative Party of BC 2026 campaign plan page on income tax (Oct 8, 2026)

positions.summary: The BC Greens propose public options and income supports to lower everyday costs, including a public grocery network and higher assistance rates.
commitments: 2026 platform: Create a network of public grocery stores ("Green Grocers"), starting with 20 stores and a distribution hub at $100 million in upfront costs, with a basket of core goods priced 30% below market.
2026 platform: Raise social assistance and disability assistance rates to the Market Basket Measure poverty line and index them to inflation (costed at about $4 billion per year).
2026 platform: Raise the minimum wage annually by inflation plus 1% until it reaches the living wage.
2026 platform: Introduce legislation within the first 100 days to ban retailers from using personal data to raise prices for individual consumers ("surveillance pricing").
positions.sourceTitle: BC Greens 2026 platform, "Believe in Better" (October 2026)

positions.summary: CentreBC would cut the lowest income tax rate, expand the renter's credit and cap Hydro and ICBC rate increases, which it estimates saves a typical two-income family about $640 a year by 2030/31.
commitments: Lower the first-bracket income tax rate from 5.6% to 5.06% on January 1, 2027 (about $540 a year for a two-income family)
Raise the renter's tax credit from $400 to $600 a year, indexed, with the full credit up to $80,000 household income and partial up to $100,000
Cap BC Hydro residential rate increases at inflation and no more than 3% a year from 2027 to 2030; hold ICBC basic rate increases at or below inflation through 2030
From April 1, 2027, publish the estimated household cost of every major new policy, fee or tax 30 days before adoption
positions.sourceTitle: CentreBC 2026 platform, A Balanced Plan for British Columbia (updated 2026-10-16)

positions.summary: OneBC's affordability measures are tax cuts and changes to auto insurance and building rules.
commitments: Cut income tax rates by 25% in every bracket
Reduce the Provincial Sales Tax (PST) by 2 percentage points
Phase out ICBC's public auto insurance monopoly and end no-fault insurance
Eliminate the BC Energy Step Code
positions.sourceTitle: OneBC, Our Priorities (party policy page, accessed Oct 2026)

positions.summary: The BC NDP says it will expand team-based primary care, add training seats and diagnostic capacity, and keep health care public, funded partly by higher taxes on top earners.
commitments: 2026 platform: Build 20 new team-based primary care clinics and offer incentives for same-day, evening and weekend appointments.
2026 platform: Add 1,000 training seats for nurses, nurse practitioners, allied health workers and care aides, including a 20% increase in nursing seats.
2026 platform: Expand MRI and CT scanning capacity in growing and rural communities and create coordinated regional surgical waitlists.
2026 platform: Phase out hospital reliance on private agency nurses over three years and close loopholes allowing user fees and extra billing.
2026 platform: Triple the U.S. health worker recruitment campaign.
positions.sourceTitle: BC NDP 2026 election platform (bcndp.ca/plan)

positions.summary: The party says it would keep health care universal and publicly funded at current funding levels while hiring more doctors and nurses to keep emergency rooms and maternity wards open.
commitments: 2026 platform: Create a $50 million emergency fund to help rural medical practices stay open and recruit staff.
2026 platform: Launch an expert commission within the first 100 days to bring proven approaches from other public systems to B.C. and reduce wait times.
2026 platform: Train more doctors in B.C., bring home Canadians who studied medicine abroad, and speed up international credential recognition.
2026 platform: Protect existing health funding so patients "never need anything more than their health card" to get care.
2026 platform: Complete the Surrey (Cloverdale) hospital and build a new Women and Children's Hospital in Surrey.
positions.sourceTitle: Conservative Party of BC 2026 campaign plan page on emergency rooms and health care (Oct 5, 2026)

positions.summary: The BC Greens propose expanding publicly delivered primary care through community health centres and oppose increased use of private care in the public system.
commitments: 2026 platform: Establish an integrated Community Health Centre in every riding in the province.
2026 platform: Cover six visits a year to a mental health professional, such as a psychologist, under the Medical Services Plan.
2026 platform: Fund nurses in the public system to support safe nurse-to-patient ratios and phase out reliance on private agency nurses and for-profit staffing agencies.
2026 platform: Make all recommended vaccines available at no cost.
2026 platform: Review the health authority model, with a focus on a consolidated health authority with localized decision-making.
positions.sourceTitle: BC Greens 2026 platform, "Believe in Better" (October 2026)

positions.summary: CentreBC commits to a family doctor or nurse practitioner team for everyone who wants one by the end of 2031, within the public system, with published wait-time targets.
commitments: Family doctor or nurse practitioner team for everyone who wants one by end of 2031; from 2029 no one waits more than 12 months
Add 600 nurse practitioner positions in the public system by 2030 and assess 200 internationally trained family doctors a year by 2028
Add 15,000 scheduled surgeries a year by 2030/31 and five MRI machines in public hospitals
Make the rural retention bonus permanent, create a $25 million a year rural ER stabilization fund and halve unplanned ER closure hours by 2029/30
positions.sourceTitle: CentreBC 2026 platform, A Balanced Plan for British Columbia (updated 2026-10-16)

positions.summary: OneBC would allow private health care alongside a fully funded public system and shift spending from administration to front-line care.
commitments: Allow private health care alongside fully funded public health care
Shift administration and human-resources spending to front-line employees and resources
Repeal the Health Professions and Occupations Act (HPOA)
Use the findings of the federal Parliament's 'Allison Inquiry' to shape BC vaccine protocols
positions.sourceTitle: OneBC, Our Priorities (party policy page, accessed Oct 2026)

positions.summary: The BC NDP's 2026 campaign commits to new school construction in growing communities; in government it added K-12 funding for teachers and specialists, and its 2024 platform set out classroom staffing commitments.
commitments: 2026 platform: Build a new middle school in Coquitlam's Burke Mountain neighbourhood.
2026 platform: Help the Iqra Education Society build a new high school in Surrey.

In government (Budget 2026): $634 million in new K-12 funding over three years, including $167 million for the Classroom Enhancement Fund for more teachers, special education teachers, psychologists and counsellors.
2024 platform: Ensure every public school has a mental health counsellor and staff each kindergarten to Grade 3 classroom with an education assistant.
2024 platform: Build more than 20,000 new student spaces at 58 K-12 projects and ban cellphone use in schools.
positions.sourceTitle: BC NDP 2026 campaign release on a Burke Mountain middle school

positions.summary: The party says it would repeal SOGI in schools while keeping schools safe, and expand trades and skills pathways for students.
commitments: 2026 platform: Repeal SOGI (sexual orientation and gender identity) in schools while "providing a safe place for our kids to go to school".
2026 platform: Expand dual-credit programs, apprenticeships and paid work experience, and make it easier for schools to hire qualified tradespeople and other experts.
2026 platform: Begin planning a new middle school on Burke Mountain (Coquitlam) and complete the 1,000-seat middle/secondary school under construction there.
2024 platform: Restore letter grades for Grades 4 to 9 and standardized provincial exams in Grades 10 and 12.
2024 platform: Open new schools as neighbourhoods grow and phase out portable classrooms.
positions.sourceTitle: Conservative Party of BC 2026 campaign plan page on schools (Oct 7, 2026)

positions.summary: The BC Greens propose a new needs-based K-12 funding model and lower costs for post-secondary students, funded partly by phasing out public funding for private schools.
commitments: 2026 platform: Eliminate the gap in inclusive (special) education funding by replacing the per-pupil formula with a needs-based model.
2026 platform: Reallocate public funding for private schools to the public system in a phased approach.
2026 platform: Create a universal school food program and a school supplies program.
2026 platform: Enact a moratorium on AI use in K-12 classrooms while provincial direction on its use is developed.
2026 platform: Freeze domestic post-secondary tuition and mandatory fees, and double the BC Access Grant to up to $8,000 per year for students with financial need.
positions.sourceTitle: BC Greens 2026 platform, "Believe in Better" (October 2026)

positions.summary: CentreBC would add school seats, counsellors and education assistants, and expand early literacy and numeracy screening.
commitments: Open 25,000 new permanent school seats by 2031 using standard designs and prefabricated additions
Reach one counsellor per 400 students and add 1,500 education assistants by 2030
Extend early screening to math for kindergarten to Grade 3 by 2028, with about 250 literacy and numeracy coaches
Restore letter grades with written comments for Grades 4 to 9 from September 2028
Expand school food programs to reach 40% of students by 2030
positions.sourceTitle: CentreBC 2026 platform, A Balanced Plan for British Columbia (updated 2026-10-16)

positions.summary: OneBC would return to standardized testing in core subjects, remove SOGI 123 from classrooms and legislate parental rights.
commitments: Bring back standardized testing focused on reading, writing and mathematics
Remove SOGI 123 and what the party calls politicized content from classrooms
Institute a Parental Bill of Rights guaranteeing informed consent and classroom transparency for parents of minor students
positions.sourceTitle: OneBC, Our Priorities (party policy page, accessed Oct 2026)

positions.summary: The BC NDP frames its economic plan as a response to U.S. tariffs, with support for small businesses, "Built in B.C." procurement rules and faster development of critical minerals and major projects.
commitments: 2026 platform: A $5,000 refundable Youth Hiring Tax Credit for small businesses that hire a person aged 18 to 30 into a first full-time, 12-month job.
2026 platform: A $500 million Small Business Tariff & Wildfire Relief Fund offering interest-free loans of up to $1 million for up to 72 months.

2026 platform: "Built in B.C. and Canada" procurement rules with minimum B.C./Canadian content for wood, steel, aluminum and cement on public projects, plus a legal requirement that next-generation ferries be built in Canada.
2026 platform: Double B.C.'s critical mineral production and exports within five years and make the BC Manufacturing Jobs Fund permanent at $60 million a year.
In government (Budget 2026): $283 million over three years for skilled trades training and a new $400 million strategic investment fund for major projects.
positions.sourceTitle: BC NDP 2026 election platform (bcndp.ca/plan)

positions.summary: The party says it would attract investment and jobs by reducing regulation, speeding up approvals for major projects and cutting taxes on business investment.
commitments: 2026 platform: Appoint a Minister for Red Tape Reduction and return regulatory requirements to 2017 levels by the end of a first term.
2026 platform: Pass a "one-in, two-out" red-tape reduction law.
2026 platform: Introduce a 120-day permitting act for major projects over $250 million.
2026 platform: Create a First Job Tax Credit for businesses that hire young British Columbians for their first job.
2026 platform: Restore the Premier's Technology Council and create a Premier's Advisory Council on Investment.
positions.sourceTitle: Conservative Party of BC campaign release on the economy (Oct 7, 2026)

positions.summary: The BC Greens propose a green industrial strategy, stronger worker bargaining rights and new protections for small businesses.
commitments: 2026 platform: Launch a green industrial strategy using public procurement, financing, training and research to build BC supply chains.
2026 platform: Pilot sectoral bargaining for workers with limited access to collective bargaining, such as migrant care, retail and food service workers.
2026 platform: Require Project Labour Agreements or Community Benefit Agreements on all public infrastructure and construction projects.
2026 platform: Introduce province-wide commercial rent protections, starting with a commercial rent registry and phased limits on rent increases.
2026 platform: Create a single front door for business approvals, coordinating provincial permits and licences behind one submission.
positions.sourceTitle: BC Greens 2026 platform, "Believe in Better" (October 2026)

positions.summary: CentreBC focuses on trade diversification, faster project approvals and support for sectors affected by US tariffs.
commitments: Double BC exports outside the US from about $31 billion (2025) to $62 billion by 2033
Cut provincial regulatory requirements by 25% by 2030, with routine permits decided within 90 days or deemed approved
Halve the Employer Health Tax for two years for tariff-affected sectors and create a $100 million supply-chain fund
Add $60 million a year for skilled trades training (about 3,500 more seats a year by 2028) and double the Manufacturing Jobs Fund to $60 million a year
Remove BC's remaining exceptions under the Canadian Free Trade Agreement by July 1, 2027
positions.sourceTitle: CentreBC 2026 platform, A Balanced Plan for British Columbia (updated 2026-10-16)

positions.summary: OneBC says government's role is to create conditions in which private business can thrive rather than to create jobs directly.
commitments: Audit BC's more than 176,000 regulations to reduce bureaucracy
Cut tax rates by 25% in every bracket, including corporate tax
Increase the allowable annual cut, reduce stumpage fees and speed up permit approvals and consultations for the forest sector
positions.sourceTitle: OneBC, Our Priorities (party policy page, accessed Oct 2026)

positions.summary: The BC NDP proposes higher income tax rates on top earners to fund health care and says it will bring the deficit down over time without cuts to health care.
commitments: 2026 platform: Raise the top two income tax bracket rates by 2 percentage points on income above $190,405 a year.
2026 platform: Create a new 24.5% bracket on income over $1,000,000 a year; the party projects $225 million in 2026-27, $925 million in 2027-28 and $1 billion from 2028-29.
2026 platform: Pause the previously announced expansion of PST to professional services; the costing plan projects deficits of $13.75 billion in 2026-27 declining to $11.97 billion in 2028-29.

In government (Budget 2026): Raised the first income tax bracket rate by less than 0.6 percentage points, paired with a larger B.C. Tax Reduction Credit, and projected deficits declining from $13.3 billion in 2026-27 to $11.4 billion in 2028-29.
positions.sourceTitle: BC NDP 2026 fiscal and costing plan

positions.summary: The party pledges not to raise or introduce taxes while in government and to reduce taxes on income and business investment.
commitments: 2026 platform: Never raise taxes on British Columbians for the entirety of a Conservative government.
2026 platform: Remove the PST on new machinery, equipment and business software (purchases and leases) for three years.
2026 platform: Appoint an expert panel to report within 180 days on simplifying B.C.'s tax system.
2024 platform: Require voter approval through a referendum or election campaign for any new tax.
positions.sourceTitle: Conservative Party of BC 2026 campaign plan page on taxes (Oct 5, 2026)

positions.summary: The BC Greens estimate their platform adds $9.28 billion a year in costs, offset by new taxes on net wealth above $50 million, higher resource royalties and higher industrial water rates; the party says no one who works for an income would pay more tax.
commitments: 2026 platform: Introduce a one-time Fair Share tax on net wealth of 5% above $50 million, 10% above $100 million and 20% above $1 billion, estimated to raise about $22.2 billion.
2026 platform: Follow with an annual wealth tax of 2% above $50 million, 3% above $100 million and 5% above $1 billion, estimated at about $5.4 billion a year.
2026 platform: Develop a progressive tax on inheritances above $10 million.
2026 platform: Establish a minimum effective provincial tax for large corporations and a temporary excess-profits tax during major disruptions.
2026 platform: Projected new revenue of $25.3 billion in 2027/28 and $9.14 billion in 2028/29.
positions.sourceTitle: BC Greens 2026 platform, "Believe in Better" (October 2026)

positions.summary: CentreBC would reduce the deficit every year after its first budget, to about $9.0 billion by 2030/31, and balance the budget by 2034/35, with the path set in law.
commitments: Balance the budget by 2034/35, with the path written into law and checked by an Independent Budget Officer
Reduce public-sector positions by 10,000 over four years through attrition, saving about $1.1 billion a year by 2030/31
Zero-based review of every ministry's administrative budget, published within 180 days of taking office
Set a 2% a year public-sector compensation mandate while the deficit comes down
Total platform cost about $13.7 billion over four years including interest, plus $7.8 billion in borrowed capital
positions.sourceTitle: CentreBC 2026 platform, A Balanced Plan for British Columbia (updated 2026-10-16)

positions.summary: OneBC would cut income, corporate and sales taxes and balance the budget within four years, directing part of any surplus to debt repayment.
commitments: Cut tax rates by 25% in every bracket, including corporate
Reduce the PST by 2 percentage points
Balance the budget within 4 years, aiming for surpluses
Put a portion of budget surpluses toward debt repayment to reduce debt-servicing costs
positions.sourceTitle: OneBC, Our Priorities (party policy page, accessed Oct 2026)

positions.summary: The BC NDP supports LNG expansion and critical mineral development alongside new transmission infrastructure, and says it will limit power supplied to new AI data centres.
commitments: 2026 platform: Fast-track the North Coast Transmission Line, using 70% Canadian steel for Phase 1 towers and 100% for Phase 2.
2026 platform: Continue supporting LNG expansion, with new LNG projects required to be net-zero-ready by 2030.
2026 platform: Maintain BC Hydro's cap on power for new AI data centres and set water-efficiency and public reporting rules for data centres.
2026 platform: Create a Clean Futures Fund with an initial $50 million funded from a portion of provincial oil and gas revenue.
positions.sourceTitle: BC NDP 2026 election platform (bcndp.ca/plan)

positions.summary: The party says it would make B.C. an "energy superpower" by expanding natural gas and LNG production with First Nations partnership and faster approvals, and would support mining and other resource sectors.
commitments: 2026 platform: Double B.C.'s natural gas/LNG production by 2032 and triple it by 2035 (BC Energy Superpower Plan).
2026 platform: Put First Nations partnership and ownership at the centre of new resource development.
2026 platform: Develop a Future Mining Jobs Blueprint with industry.
2024 platform: Amend the Clean Energy Act to allow nuclear power, with a small modular reactor operating by 2035 if the business case, seismic safety and public confidence are met.
positions.sourceTitle: Conservative Party of BC 2026 campaign plan page on energy (Oct 5, 2026)

positions.summary: The BC Greens propose ending expansion of oil and gas, collecting higher royalties on existing production, and expanding renewable electricity and community-owned energy.
commitments: 2026 platform: End approvals for new fracking expansion, LNG terminals and expansions, and new fossil fuel pipelines.
2026 platform: Reform oil and gas royalties to collect 50% of net profits, estimated at about $4.09 billion in natural gas royalties in 2027/28, nearly $3 billion more than forecast.
2026 platform: Set a target for electricity to supply at least 35% of BC's total energy needs by 2035, with no new large hydroelectric dams.
2026 platform: Restore one-for-one net metering for household solar and legalize certified plug-in balcony solar.
2026 platform: Reject the proposed Working Forest Model and its 45 million cubic metre harvest objective, and end raw-log exports.
positions.sourceTitle: BC Greens 2026 platform, "Believe in Better" (October 2026)

positions.summary: CentreBC supports LNG projects with First Nations partners, new mines and higher timber harvests, and would expand BC Hydro capacity.
commitments: Back LNG projects with First Nations partners and a plan to be net-zero ready; keep industrial carbon pricing with no consumer carbon tax
Make permitting decisions on 10 new mines by 2030, targeting 3 processing facilities by 2032
Expand BC Hydro by at least 2,000 megawatts by 2033
Work toward a 45 million cubic metre timber harvest, reaching 40 million by 2030; grow BC Timber Sales to 9 million cubic metres a year by 2029
One coordinated review with a 12-month deadline for provincial major-project decisions
positions.sourceTitle: CentreBC 2026 platform, A Balanced Plan for British Columbia (updated 2026-10-16)

positions.summary: OneBC supports a pipeline to a northern BC port and more timber harvesting, and would co-operate with Alberta and Saskatchewan on energy projects.
commitments: Approve a pipeline to the Port of Prince Rupert or Kitimat to move Canadian energy to foreign markets
Increase the allowable annual cut for the forest sector
Reduce stumpage fees for lumber companies
Adopt the Western Canada Alliance plan to work with Alberta and Saskatchewan on Western Canadian interests and energy projects
positions.sourceTitle: OneBC, Our Priorities (party policy page, accessed Oct 2026)

positions.summary: The BC NDP commits to expanding protected areas, funding old-growth and watershed protection, and supporting household energy upgrades and methane reductions.
commitments: 2026 platform: Protect 30% of B.C.'s land by 2030, including a Northwest Critical Conservation Corridor.
2026 platform: A new $50 million fund to convert old-growth deferrals into permanent protection, and an additional $30 million a year for the B.C. Watershed Security Fund.
2026 platform: Work to virtually eliminate methane emissions by 2035, building on the 75%-by-2030 target.
2026 platform: $50 million a year in heat pump rebates and $16 million a year to triple public EV charging ports over a decade.
2026 platform: $4 million a year to double the Youth Climate Corps for ages 17 to 30.
positions.sourceTitle: BC NDP 2026 election platform (bcndp.ca/plan)

positions.summary: The party's 2026 environmental commitments focus on wildfire prevention and response; its 2024 platform called for removing carbon pricing and reversing restrictions on natural gas heating and non-electric vehicles.
commitments: 2026 platform: Make immediate down payments on a B.C.-owned fleet of water bombers and other firefighting aircraft, leasing them to other jurisdictions in winter to offset costs.
2026 platform: Reduce forest fuels around communities and make prescribed burning easier to use without lowering safety standards.
2026 platform: Create a dedicated fund for wildfire early-detection and prevention technologies.
2024 platform: Repeal all carbon taxes, including carbon pricing on industry.
2024 platform: Reverse plans to ban natural gas heating and non-electric vehicles.
positions.sourceTitle: Conservative Party of BC 2026 campaign plan page on wildfires (Oct 5, 2026)

positions.summary: The BC Greens propose a new climate plan with sector-by-sector milestones and binding accountability, along with permanent protection of old-growth forests.
commitments: 2026 platform: Bring in a new provincial climate action plan with sector milestones and annual public reporting, keeping the legislated 2040 and 2050 targets and adding interim targets.
2026 platform: Restore the requirement that 100% of new light-duty vehicle sales be zero-emission by 2035.
2026 platform: Enforce a province-wide ban on gas hookups in all new buildings.
2026 platform: Permanently protect big-treed old growth and large second-growth forests and implement all 14 recommendations of the Old Growth Strategic Review.
2026 platform: Protect at least 30% of BC's lands and waters by 2030, working with First Nations and the federal government.
positions.sourceTitle: BC Greens 2026 platform, "Believe in Better" (October 2026)

positions.summary: CentreBC would legislate a 2030 emissions milestone of 20% below 2007 levels, keep the 2040 and 2050 targets and create an independent Climate Accountability Office.
commitments: Set in law a 2030 milestone of 20% below 2007 emissions, keeping 2040 and 2050 targets
Hold an annual competitive call for at least 3,000 GWh of clean power, with First Nations partners in every winning project
Legislate a 75% cut in oil and gas methane below 2014 levels by 2030
Offer home energy upgrade loans repaid over up to 20 years through property tax or Hydro bills (about 25,000 homes by 2030/31)
Install highway fast chargers at least every 80 km on main highways by 2030 (about 1,500 ports)
positions.sourceTitle: CentreBC 2026 platform, A Balanced Plan for British Columbia (updated 2026-10-16)

positions.summary: No specific commitment published.
positions.sourceTitle: OneBC, Our Priorities (party policy page, accessed Oct 2026)

positions.summary: The BC NDP focuses on repeat offenders, gangs, extortion and retail theft through targeted policing programs, more prosecutors and asset seizure.
commitments: 2026 platform: Make the ReVOII and C-POII repeat-offender programs permanent and double their funding.
2026 platform: Hire 50 more Crown prosecutors and create a unit for extortion, racketeering and gang violence.
2026 platform: Create a BC Retail Theft Task Force with RCMP, municipal and federal police.

2026 platform: Seize gang assets such as vehicles, properties and front businesses, and impose immediate penalties such as driving suspensions and business-licence loss for illegal gun or gang activity.
In government (Budget 2026): $139 million over three years to reduce repeat violent offending and chronic property crime and support timely access to justice.
positions.sourceTitle: BC NDP 2026 election platform (bcndp.ca/plan)

positions.summary: The party says it would add police, prosecutors and court capacity and focus on repeat and violent offenders, gangs and extortion.
commitments: 2026 platform: Hire and deploy 250 more police officers by expanding the JIBC Police Academy, and add 500 RCMP officers and 150 civilian staff in rural and regional communities over five years.
2026 platform: Hire 50 new Crown prosecutors and work with Ottawa to fund 20 more trial judges.
2026 platform: Create a dedicated repeat-offender court stream, strengthen bail and warrant enforcement, and expand electronic monitoring.
2026 platform: Implement an Anti-Extortion Action Plan with dedicated investigators.
2026 platform: Publicly report results on repeat offending, bail compliance, court delays and treatment access.
positions.sourceTitle: Conservative Party of BC 2026 campaign plan page on public safety (Oct 6, 2026)

positions.summary: The BC Greens propose reforming policing and justice institutions with a focus on accountability, and shifting mental health and substance-use calls away from police.
commitments: 2026 platform: Enact a new Community Safety and Policing Act, following the Transforming Policing and Community Safety in British Columbia committee report.
2026 platform: Add mental health as a fourth option in 911 alongside police, fire and ambulance, and expand funding for community-led crisis response teams.
2026 platform: Disband the RCMP's Critical Response Unit (CRU-BC).
2026 platform: Create an independent, Indigenous-overseen taskforce to investigate open and cold cases of violence against Indigenous women, children and Two-Spirit people.
2026 platform: Require all police services to collect and publicly report disaggregated race-based data.
positions.sourceTitle: BC Greens 2026 platform, "Believe in Better" (October 2026)

positions.summary: CentreBC would add provincial RCMP officers and Crown prosecutors and fund downtown safety teams, with a quarterly public safety dashboard.
commitments: Hire 100 additional provincial RCMP officers a year for five years (500 total)
Add 60 Crown prosecutors with support staff by 2030/31 and make the extortion task force permanent
Fund safety and outreach teams in 20 BC downtowns by 2028
Hold an independent review of bail in BC and publish quarterly bail data
Restore FireSmart grants to $40 million a year, guaranteed in law for five years
positions.sourceTitle: CentreBC 2026 platform, A Balanced Plan for British Columbia (updated 2026-10-16)

positions.summary: OneBC would focus the justice system on repeat and violent offenders and opposes provincial participation in federal firearms buy-back programs.
commitments: Focus criminal justice resources on repeat and violent offenders
Instruct prosecutors to treat past charges or convictions as an indicator of future danger to the public
Work with the federal government against international smuggling of drugs and firearms through ports
No provincial participation in any federal buy-back or confiscation of legally acquired firearms, with provincial legal representation and a provincial storage program for affected owners
Prohibit wearing masks during protests
positions.sourceTitle: OneBC, Our Priorities (party policy page, accessed Oct 2026)

positions.summary: The BC NDP commits to a province-wide network of involuntary care centres alongside expanded voluntary treatment; in government it did not renew the drug decriminalization exemption, which expired January 31, 2026.
commitments: 2026 platform: Invest up to $90 million to establish involuntary care at the Okanagan Correctional Centre in Oliver, as part of a network of involuntary care centres across the province including Surrey and Prince George.
2026 platform: Double the number of youth treatment beds and make Access Central same-day clinical assessments available in every health authority.

In government (Budget 2026): $131 million for intensive mental health and addictions treatment for people with complex mental illness, addictions and brain injuries, including involuntary treatment beds in Prince George, Maple Ridge and Surrey.
In government (2026): The federal exemption decriminalizing possession of small amounts of certain drugs in B.C. expired on January 31, 2026, and the Province did not renew it.
positions.sourceTitle: BC NDP 2026 campaign release on involuntary care (Oct 16, 2026)

positions.summary: The party says it would end prescribed "safe supply", expand treatment and recovery, and allow mandatory treatment for people with severe addiction, mental illness or brain injury.
commitments: 2026 platform: Provide "compassionate intervention" to move people with severe addiction, mental illness or brain injury off the street and into care.
2026 platform: Amend the Mental Health Act so police can connect people with mandatory treatment.
2026 platform: End the "safe supply" program and stop illegal drug use in hospitals, shelters and publicly funded supportive housing.
2026 platform: Expand psychiatric services, crisis response and residential treatment, and expand access to naloxone.
positions.sourceTitle: Conservative Party of BC 2026 campaign plan page on public safety and addiction (Oct 6, 2026)

positions.summary: The BC Greens describe drug use as a health and social issue and propose regulated alternatives to the illicit supply, decriminalization of personal possession and expanded treatment.
commitments: 2026 platform: Provide regulated pharmaceutical alternatives to the illicit drug supply, based on advice from health professionals.
2026 platform: Decriminalize possession of drugs for personal use.
2026 platform: Expand supervised consumption and overdose prevention sites, including inhalation spaces and mobile and 24-hour sites.
2026 platform: Match investments in bed-based treatment with community-based outpatient treatment services, and set an evidence-based standard of care for all treatment services.
2026 platform: Provide annual funding for existing drug-checking services.
positions.sourceTitle: BC Greens 2026 platform, "Believe in Better" (October 2026)

positions.summary: CentreBC would expand publicly funded detox and treatment with published wait times, ask Ottawa to charge public drug possession, and amend involuntary care rules under the Mental Health Act.
commitments: Add 150 detox beds and 500 treatment and recovery beds by 2030; same-day detox for urgent cases by 2028 and treatment within 14 days by 2030
Within 100 days, ask Ottawa to change the federal prosecution directive so public drug possession and possession by repeat offenders is charged
Amend the Mental Health Act to assess each patient's capacity individually while keeping secure involuntary care, and expand the Red Fish Healing Centre by about 50 beds from 2029
Offer voluntary addiction treatment in every provincial correctional centre by 2029
positions.sourceTitle: CentreBC 2026 platform, A Balanced Plan for British Columbia (updated 2026-10-16)

positions.summary: OneBC would end safe supply and supervised consumption programs and move to involuntary treatment and recovery.
commitments: Eliminate safe supply and drug consumption programs
Cancel all new drug consumption sites and convert existing sites into recovery centres
Provide involuntary drug rehabilitation and housing for people with severe addiction
Roll back all decriminalization programs and enforce against public drug use
positions.sourceTitle: OneBC, Our Priorities (party policy page, accessed Oct 2026)

positions.summary: The BC NDP presents partnership with First Nations on major projects and conservation as central to its plan. In government it committed in April 2026 to work with First Nations on its legal concerns about DRIPA rather than amend the Act that spring.
commitments: 2026 platform: Partner with First Nations to speed up clean energy and resource projects and share in their benefits, including First Nations participation in critical minerals development.
2026 platform: Finalize and jointly manage the Great Bear Sea National Marine Conservation Area Reserve with the federal government and six coastal First Nations.
2026 platform: Work with First Nations on watershed protection, forest restoration and emergency planning.

In government (April 20, 2026 statement with the First Nations Leadership Council): No legislation to suspend or amend DRIPA in the spring 2026 session; work with First Nations leaders to find solutions to the government's legal concerns before the fall legislative session.
positions.sourceTitle: BC NDP 2026 election platform (bcndp.ca/plan)

positions.summary: The party says it would repeal the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (DRIPA) and pursue "economic reconciliation" through First Nations partnerships and ownership in resource projects.
commitments: 2026 platform: Repeal DRIPA, section 8.1 of the Interpretation Act and the government's current litigation directions.
2026 platform: Restore the section 35 constitutional framework to provide certainty for resource development.
2026 platform: Build projects "together with First Nations", with First Nations partnership and ownership at the centre of new development.
2024 platform: Provide loan guarantees to help First Nations acquire equity in natural resource and other major projects.
2024 platform: Transfer authority for child welfare and family services to First Nations.
positions.sourceTitle: Conservative Party of BC 2026 campaign plan page on DRIPA and reconciliation (Oct 7, 2026)

positions.summary: The BC Greens say they recognize the inherent rights and title of Indigenous peoples and propose implementing the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act through further legislation.
commitments: 2026 platform: Implement the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (DRIPA) through legislation and fund public education on DRIPA.
2026 platform: Enact an Indigenous Languages Act with funding for language revitalization, and allow Indigenous languages on government-issued identification.
2026 platform: Co-develop a mechanism with Indigenous peoples to resolve Indigenous-Crown disputes without litigation.
2026 platform: Re-establish the Legislative Assembly's Aboriginal Affairs Standing Committee, supported by a public expert advisory committee.
2026 platform: Work with the federal government so Indigenous governments have stable revenue comparable to other governments.
positions.sourceTitle: BC Greens 2026 platform, "Believe in Better" (October 2026)

positions.summary: CentreBC says it respects UNDRIP as a guide and would replace DRIPA with a law built on negotiated modern treaties, while protecting private land.
commitments: In its first session, repeal DRIPA and section 8.1 of the Interpretation Act and replace them with a treaty-based law putting $30 million a year into treaty talks
Exclude private land from any agreement with a First Nation without the owner's agreement; pass a law compensating homeowners for value lost due to an Aboriginal title ruling
Expand the First Nations Equity Financing Program to $3 billion in loan guarantees within six months
Publish draft agreements at least 60 days before signing
End long-term drinking water advisories in First Nations communities by 2029, with a $25 million a year provincial top-up
positions.sourceTitle: CentreBC 2026 platform, A Balanced Plan for British Columbia (updated 2026-10-16)

positions.summary: OneBC would repeal the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (DRIPA) and seek to place all British Columbians under one legal and political framework.
commitments: Repeal DRIPA and declare UNDRIP to have no force or effect in BC (the party's proposed Property Rights Protection Act)
Halt voluntary transfers of cash, land and control over public resources to band governments, and restore oversight of band spending
Seek constitutional reforms to repeal the Indian Act and convert reserves into townships
Restore original names of public institutions and places, primarily in English, and end mandatory land acknowledgements in government-funded institutions
positions.sourceTitle: OneBC, Our Priorities (party policy page, accessed Oct 2026)

positions.summary: The BC NDP proposes more funding for BC Transit, rapid bus service in Metro Vancouver, and changes to ferry reservations and shipbuilding.
commitments: 2026 platform: Increase BC Transit funding by $40 million a year.
2026 platform: Deliver Rapid Bus Transit in Metro Vancouver with the federal government and TransLink, and develop a long-term TransLink revenue model that does not raise costs for drivers.
2026 platform: Launch a "Locals First" ferry reservation pilot on the Horseshoe Bay–Langdale and Westview–Little River routes.
2026 platform: Require by law that next-generation BC Ferries vessels be built in Canada, with up to $250 million toward a new B.C. shipyard.
positions.sourceTitle: BC NDP 2026 election platform (bcndp.ca/plan)

positions.summary: The party says it would build major highway and bridge projects, including a bridge to replace the George Massey Tunnel, and set service standards for BC Ferries.
commitments: 2026 platform: Build a 10-lane bridge to replace the George Massey Tunnel.
2026 platform: Create a BC Ferries Charter with standards for reliability, on-time performance, capacity, affordability and customer service, and seek B.C.'s share of federal ferry funding.
2024 platform: Expand Highway 1 to six lanes to Chilliwack.
2024 platform: Extend SkyTrain to Newton in Surrey along the King George corridor.
2024 platform: Never implement road tolls or bridge tolls.
positions.sourceTitle: Conservative Party of BC campaign release on the Massey crossing and Surrey hospitals (Oct 15, 2026)

positions.summary: The BC Greens propose expanding public transit toward free fares, a province-wide intercity bus network, increased ferry funding and passenger rail.
commitments: 2026 platform: Double the number of buses on the road within the first term and phase in free transit, starting with people under 25 and seniors 65 and over.
2026 platform: Build a wheelchair-accessible intercity network with at least hourly service for 80% of BC and at least daily service everywhere.
2026 platform: Bring SkyTrain to UBC and run regional transit buses on Highway 99 in the Sea-to-Sky within the first year.
2026 platform: Seek federal ferry funding parity with Atlantic Canada and re-establish the 13 Ferry Advisory Committees.
2026 platform: Develop a passenger rail strategy with First Nations focused on Vancouver Island, Metro Vancouver, the Sea-to-Sky and the Fraser Valley.
positions.sourceTitle: BC Greens 2026 platform, "Believe in Better" (October 2026)

positions.summary: CentreBC proposes a $15 billion three-year transportation plan, more transit service and a refundable commuter credit.
commitments: Deliver a $15 billion three-year plan including Surrey-Langley SkyTrain, the Fraser River Tunnel, widening Highway 1 to Chilliwack and North Coast roads
Fund a 15% increase in transit service by 2030 with TransLink and BC Transit, including about six new rapid bus lines
Create a refundable BC Commuter Credit of 15% on monthly and annual transit passes and BC Ferries multi-trip fares
Rebuild rural intercity bus service from 2029
Match a requested $1.5 billion federal contribution for Prince Rupert and Roberts Bank port capacity with $750 million in road and rail connections over five years
positions.sourceTitle: CentreBC 2026 platform, A Balanced Plan for British Columbia (updated 2026-10-16)

positions.summary: No specific commitment published.
positions.sourceTitle: OneBC, Our Priorities (party policy page, accessed Oct 2026)

positions.summary: The BC NDP commits to expanding affordable child care, including school-based before- and after-school care, and to a universal fee cap.
commitments: 2026 platform: $80 million to create 7,200 before- and after-school child care spaces on school grounds.
2026 platform: $250 million in new provincial funding to leverage federal dollars for universal child care expansion.
2026 platform: A hard, universal child care fee cap modelled on Ontario's, and a provincial wage grid for early childhood educators.
In government (Budget 2026): A $330 million increase to ChildCareBC to maintain lower fees, plus $25 million to expand child care on school grounds.
positions.sourceTitle: BC NDP 2026 campaign release on child care (Oct 17, 2026)

positions.summary: The party says it would keep $10-a-day child care while widening access through independent providers and more choice for families; its 2026 campaign adds commitments on autism funding.
commitments: 2026 platform: Extend the Autism Funding Program and review the move of autism support to the Disability Benefit and Disability Supplement.
2024 platform: Expand $10-a-day child care by ending what it calls a funding bias against independent child care providers.
2024 platform: Review and increase the Affordable Child Care Benefit and BC Family Benefit for lower- and middle-income families.
2024 platform: Create 24-hour child care spaces for shift workers and first responders.
positions.sourceTitle: Conservative Party of BC 2024 election platform (child care section)

positions.summary: The BC Greens propose expanding $10-a-day child care toward universal coverage and introducing a wage grid for early childhood educators.
commitments: 2026 platform: Lift the freeze on new $10-a-day enrolments introduced in Budget 2026 and implement universal child care coverage by 2031.
2026 platform: Create a single province-wide registration point for $10-a-day spaces, replacing centre-by-centre waitlists.
2026 platform: Implement an early childhood educator wage grid reaching $35 to $45 per hour by 2028.
2026 platform: Provide a basic income at the poverty line to all youth formerly in government care until age 25 (costed at $250 million a year).
2026 platform: Give kinship-care families the same financial and social supports that foster families receive.
positions.sourceTitle: BC Greens 2026 platform, "Believe in Better" (October 2026)

positions.summary: CentreBC would add $10-a-day child care spaces and fund early intervention and family support.
commitments: Create 20,000 new $10-a-day child care spaces by 2030, starting where waitlists are longest
Invest $100 million a year in family support and early intervention by 2030/31
Extend the rent supplement for young adults leaving care from two years to age 27
Pay a $400 a month BC Caregiver Benefit to about 9,000 low- and modest-income family caregivers of high-need people
positions.sourceTitle: CentreBC 2026 platform, A Balanced Plan for British Columbia (updated 2026-10-16)

positions.summary: No specific commitment published.
positions.sourceTitle: OneBC, Our Priorities (party policy page, accessed Oct 2026)

positions.summary: The BC NDP's seniors plan centres on more home care, free shingles vaccines and added medical services in long-term care homes.
commitments: 2026 platform: Add 500 home care workers and eliminate home care user fees.
2026 platform: Expand virtual Long-term Care at Home monitoring to about 5,600 more seniors.
2026 platform: Fully cover the two-dose shingles vaccine for adults 50 and over and immunocompromised adults.
2026 platform: Bring more nurse practitioners, pharmacy services and virtual specialist consultations into long-term care homes.
2026 platform: Bring 5,000 care-home workers into the public health employer system.
positions.sourceTitle: BC NDP 2026 election platform (bcndp.ca/plan)

positions.summary: The party says it would build long-term care beds faster and give seniors more choice in care and support to stay in their homes.
commitments: 2026 platform: Build more long-term care beds faster, including by cutting design rules for care homes while protecting safety.
2026 platform: Give seniors on waitlists portable public funding to use at qualified care providers, including non-government providers.
2026 platform: Reverse recent changes to the property tax deferment program.
2024 platform: Deliver 5,000 long-term care beds province-wide by 2030.
2024 platform: Double the Home Renovation Tax Credit for Seniors and Persons with Disabilities to $2,000 and update SAFER rent assistance thresholds annually.
positions.sourceTitle: Conservative Party of BC campaign release on long-term care (Oct 9, 2026)

positions.summary: The BC Greens propose expanding rent assistance for seniors and shifting toward more home support, while increasing publicly funded long-term care.
commitments: 2026 platform: Raise Shelter Aid for Elderly Renters (SAFER) income thresholds to $48,000 for single people and $53,000 for couples.
2026 platform: Apply vacancy control to assisted living, including additional service fees.
2026 platform: Develop and implement a plan to increase the number of publicly funded long-term care facilities.
2026 platform: Improve access to respite care, day programs and at-home care, and develop a rural seniors strategy and a dementia support strategy.
Through the 2024-2026 co-operation accord (per the party): worked with government in 2025 to raise the SAFER income limit to $40,000, adding about 1,600 seniors.
positions.sourceTitle: BC Greens 2026 platform, "Believe in Better" (October 2026)

positions.summary: CentreBC would expand home support, reduce home support fees for low-income seniors and speed up long-term care construction.
commitments: Add 1.5 million home support hours a year by 2029/30
Cut home support fees in half for low-income seniors
Build about 500 prefabricated long-term care beds in Abbotsford by 2029/30 and restart six other paused projects
Have 2,500 new long-term care beds under construction and 1,000 open by March 2031
Publish quality and staffing results for every care home every year
positions.sourceTitle: CentreBC 2026 platform, A Balanced Plan for British Columbia (updated 2026-10-16)

positions.summary: No specific commitment published.
positions.sourceTitle: OneBC, Our Priorities (party policy page, accessed Oct 2026)

positions.summary: The BC NDP says it will reduce the deficit over time and cut administrative spending; in government it set targets to reduce the size of the public sector.
commitments: 2026 platform: Bring down the deficit over time without health care cuts, as set out in the BC Strong Fiscal & Costing Plan.
2026 platform: Give Surrey its own municipal charter with authority similar to Vancouver's.
In government (Budget 2026): Targets to reduce the size of the public sector through an efficiency review, hiring restrictions and streamlined program delivery.

2024 platform: Create a standardized province-wide online municipal building permit system and unify provincial enforcement teams for gambling, liquor, traffic, transit police and tobacco into one agency.
positions.sourceTitle: BC NDP 2026 fiscal and costing plan

positions.summary: The party says it would legally separate provincial and municipal elections and increase transparency and value-for-money reviews in government.
commitments: 2026 platform: Pass a Respect Local Democracy Act so provincial and municipal elections are never held in the same fall, and no provincial election can be held within 60 days of a municipal election.
2024 platform: Conduct a "Respect for Taxpayers Audit" to identify waste and improve front-line service delivery.
2024 platform: Expand voluntary and mandatory disclosure of government information to reduce the need for freedom-of-information requests.
2024 platform: Open public infrastructure procurement to all qualified contractors and workers.
positions.sourceTitle: Conservative Party of BC campaign release on election timing (Oct 14, 2026)

positions.summary: The BC Greens propose changing the voting system to proportional representation and expanding access to government information.
commitments: 2026 platform: Introduce legislation within the first 100 days to implement proportional representation for the 2030 election.
2026 platform: Extend voting rights to 16- and 17-year-olds.
2026 platform: Establish a biennial citizens' assembly on topics chosen by the Legislative Assembly.
2026 platform: Remove the fee for Freedom of Information requests and repeal the changes made by the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Amendment Act, 2026.
2026 platform: Enforce a minimum two-year period between holding a designated government office and lobbying.
positions.sourceTitle: BC Greens 2026 platform, "Believe in Better" (October 2026)

positions.summary: CentreBC would expand public reporting, remove the freedom-of-information fee and create an Independent Budget Officer.
commitments: Eliminate the $10 freedom-of-information fee on day one, clear the overdue backlog by 2028 and answer 90% of requests on time within two years
Publish contracts and project agreements over $10 million in full within 30 days
Create an Independent Budget Officer reporting to the legislature
Track platform commitments quarterly, with the Auditor General checking the numbers annually
Introduce a Trustworthy Government AI Act by spring 2027 requiring human review of significant automated decisions
positions.sourceTitle: CentreBC 2026 platform, A Balanced Plan for British Columbia (updated 2026-10-16)

positions.summary: OneBC would reduce provincial regulation and seek a formal alliance with Alberta and Saskatchewan on provincial jurisdiction.
commitments: Adopt the Western Canada Alliance plan with Alberta and Saskatchewan to strengthen provincial sovereignty and bargaining position
Audit BC's more than 176,000 regulations
End mandatory land acknowledgements in government and government-funded institutions
positions.sourceTitle: OneBC, Our Priorities (party policy page, accessed Oct 2026)
